content: 1. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and caution should be exercised. 2. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of warfarin through mechanisms involving other pathways. Warfarin's less potent R-enantiomer is partially metabolized by CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19. Frequent monitoring of INR is necessary when co-administered with inhibitors of these enzymes, and warfarin dosage adjustments may be required. 3. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 4. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 5. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, and close monitoring is required. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt zanubrutinib dosing as recommended for adverse reactions, and resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 6. Indinavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 7. Indinavir increases the levels of zileuton by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase toxicity risk, so close monitoring and caution are necessary. 8. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 9. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 10. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 11. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, and close monitoring is required. Reduce the zuranolone dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 12. Indinavir is associated with nephrolithiasis or urolithiasis in 29% of pediatric patients and 12% of adults. Other adverse effects include hyperbilirubinemia (14%), nausea (12%), pain (17%), abdominal pain (9%), thrombocytopenia (1%), back pain (8%), dysuria (2%), headache (6%), fever (2%), dizziness (3%), diarrhea/vomiting (4-5%), weakness (4%), malaise (2%), insomnia (3%), fatigue (2%), taste perversion (3%), flank pain (3%), pruritus (4%), neutropenia (2%), cough (2%), and angina. 13. Rare but serious adverse effects include erythema multiforme, hepatitis, crystalluria, angina, fat redistribution, cardiovascular disorders (e.g., myocardial infarction, angina pectoris, cerebrovascular disorders), liver function abnormalities, pancreatitis, jaundice, abdominal distension, dyspepsia, increased spontaneous bleeding in hemophilia patients, acute hemolytic anemia, new-onset diabetes mellitus, hyperglycemia, anaphylactoid reactions, urticaria, vasculitis, arthralgia, periarthritis, oral paresthesia, depression, rash (including Stevens-Johnson syndrome), hyperpigmentation, alopecia, ingrown toenails, paronychia, nephritis, pyelonephritis, renal insufficiency, renal failure, leukocyturia, crystalluria, and dysuria. 14. Laboratory abnormalities include increased serum triglycerides and cholesterol levels. 15. Indinavir is contraindicated with certain drugs, including alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonists (e.g., alfuzosin), antiarrhythmics (e.g., amiodarone, flecainide, propafenone, quinidine), rifampin, voriconazole, ergot derivatives (e.g., dihydroergotamine, ergotamine), cisapride, and St. John’s Wort. 16. To reduce the risk of nephrolithiasis or urolithiasis, patients should maintain adequate hydration (e.g., at least 1.5 liters of liquids per day), especially in children who are at higher risk. 17. Indinavir use may lead to fat redistribution, hemolytic anemia, hyperglycemia, hyperbilirubinemia, and immune reconstitution syndrome when combined with other antiretroviral drugs. 18. Indinavir should be separated from didanosine by at least one hour. Liver function tests (LFTs) should be monitored every 6-12 weeks. 19. Indinavir is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Its excretion in breast milk is unknown, and it is contraindicated during lactation. 20. Indinavir is primarily excreted in feces (83%) and urine (19%). It should be taken on an empty stomach with water, one hour before or two hours after a meal. It may be taken with skim milk or a low-fat meal. When co-administered with ritonavir, it can be taken without regard to meals.
